title: Fidget and the Whispering Wind Weasel
markdown:
In Aeridor the towers scraped cloud, and Fidget the goblin wore hair like damp moss and a grin that threatened the rest of his face. Nettle the mouse had whiskers with opinions and a tail that could untie a dragon’s bootlace if the dragon had been careless. Other goblins hoarded pebbles. Fidget collected the peculiar. Griffins glittered. Grumble-cats purred. He wanted the creature everyone else wrinkled their noses at.

“A Whispering Wind Weasel?” Hamish Bumble, the baker, scoffed. His eyebrows were startled caterpillars. “Flighty. It will steal your best spoon. Then you will eat stew with your hands.” His laugh sounded like flour deciding to be weather.

“They sing at dawn,” said the Mayor, hat already tilted for a gust. “Unsettling. A scone deserves peace.”

Fidget was smitten. The weasel’s fur was moonlight that had learned to run; its eyes were stars that had not asked permission. He named it Zephyr. Zephyr preferred serenading the moon with trills that had not been invited to Fidget’s lumpy berry stew. It vanished for hours and reappeared on the highest spire, unimpressed.

“Misunderstood,” Fidget told Nettle, who was mending a sock with a hole the size of a principle.

“Or ornery,” Nettle squeaked. “It is judging hats.”

At the Stone Keep, Grumblebelly the Guard Troll doted on Fluffernutter, a prize cloud-sheep: pink, vast, a marshmallow that could out-stubborn a hurricane.

“Come, fluffy blossom. Extra-fluffy carrots. The Pet Parade.”

Fluffernutter became a pink boulder and blinked vacant poetry.

Then a rogue wind—not Zephyr’s—tore through the square like a toddler with a title. It snatched the Mayor’s jeweled hat toward the Whispering Peaks. She shrieked like a goose that had read a will. Grumblebelly roared like an avalanche that had stubbed a toe.

“The Duke of Dimplebottom’s gift!”

The troll moved to scale mountains. Fluffernutter planted itself in front of him. “NO. I AM A STATUE NOW.”

Fidget had failed at training Zephyr. The weasel, however, found things. Fidget built things from scraps: once a kite from a picnic blanket and a squirrel with a work ethic.

“Workshop,” he told Nettle, charcoal already sketching. Vine. Discarded dragon scales. A whistle that sounded like angry geese being tickled. Nettle fetched hammer, sap, scissors, and the look of someone who would later say she had known.

While Grumblebelly wrestled his pink roadblock, they ran for the Peaks. Zephyr, bored and halfway up a cliff, shimmered. Fidget clicked like a woodpecker. The weasel paused.

“The hat.”

A tail-flick, and Zephyr went into the rocks.

Fidget made a spring-net: scales to slide, vine to hold. The hat teetered on a ledge above an unhelpful drop. Then a bleat. Fluffernutter had followed, found a perfect stubbornness, and blocked the aim.

“Move, you pink puddle.”

The sheep blinked, a monument. Fidget remembered Nettle: work with the obstacle. Zephyr was chasing a butterfly. Resourcefulness was a goblin’s better habit.

He blew the whistle: a piercing note that turned Zephyr into a yelping snowball of fur. Then squeaks like juiciest mountain clover. Fluffernutter’s ears rose. A shift. Then a warble Zephyr loved, wind-chimes with ideas.

Zephyr streaked down, nudged the sheep—playful, rude, effective. Fluffernutter stepped. Then again. Reluctant. Real.

Fidget launched the net. It snagged the hat a breath before the chasm collected a Duke’s opinion.

The crowd, who had followed the now-mobile sheep, made a noise like relief trying to be dignified. The Mayor snatched the hat, gratitude mixed with the bewilderment of someone saved by the wrong sort of pet. Nettle’s tail jigged. Grumblebelly got Fluffernutter walking, though the sheep now followed Zephyr at a stubborn, respectable distance.

“Not subtle,” the troll said of the nudge. “A chaos agent.”

Later Zephyr sat on Fidget’s shoulder and groomed as if heroism were lint. The Mayor adjusted her hat. “Some pets are unconventional. Some goblins too.”

Nettle polished a tiny badge: a weasel juggling a hat. Fluffernutter decided heroism was tiring and became a nap. Fidget’s grin, for once, had somewhere useful to go.
audience: children aged 9-10, amusing mountain adventure fantasy for ages 9-10
